title: CmdPal: Reloads an icon on every command change, even when the icon doesn’t change

judgment.rationale: The report has concrete reproduction and existing upstream ownership. Preserve the covering candidate and validate the reported behavior and its controls rather than create a competing implementation or request an unnecessary diagnostics archive.
judgment.recommended_action: Review and verify the existing open candidate51926; retain this issue until a confirmed repair is available.
evidence: The report supplies the exact home fallback scenario: edit cmd /c echo hello arguments while an item keeps its own icon and replaces its Command.
The timeline links open51926, whose description explicitly closes51922.
The candidate compares the effective displayed icon around command replacement and forwarded icon changes, preserving item-icon precedence.
Added tests cover unchanged-item-icon replacement and command icon forwarding; no local notification-count or UI execution is claimed.

Run the candidate item/command icon-precedence and forwarding tests; confirm a real effective icon change still notifies.
